title: Digital Technology and Culture - Digital Cinema, Sound, and Animation Option (Pullman only)
sourceText:
DTC 101 [ARTS]

ENGLISH 101 [WRTG]

Quantitative Reasoning [QUAN]

Foreign Language, if needed, or Electives
Electives must include sufficient 300-400-level coursework to meet the University requirement of 40 credits of upper-division coursework. May need to include a writing in the major [M] course to meet University requirements.
Two years of high school foreign language or at least two semesters of college-level foreign language are required by the College of Arts and Sciences for graduation.

Communication [COMM] or Written Communication [WRTG]

DTC 201

HISTORY 105 [ROOT]

Biological Sciences [BSCI] with lab
To meet College of Arts and Sciences requirements, students must complete 1 additional lab credit of [BSCI] or [PSCI] for a total of 8 credits (2 labs).

DTC 206 [EQJS] or 475 [DIVR]

Humanities [HUM]

Electives
Electives must include sufficient 300-400-level coursework to meet the University requirement of 40 credits of upper-division coursework. May need to include a writing in the major [M] course to meet University requirements.

DTC 208

Physical Science [PSCI] with lab
To meet College of Arts and Sciences requirements, students must complete 1 additional lab credit of [BSCI] or [PSCI] for a total of 8 credits (2 labs).

Social Sciences [SSCI]

Complete Writing Portfolio

DTC 335

DTC 354 [M]

Equity and Justice [EQJS] or Diversity [DIVR]
Depending on whether a student takes DTC 206 [EQJS] or DTC 475 [DIVR] for their degree requirement, they should take a UCORE option that fulfills the opposite requirement in their third year.

DTC 301 [M]

DTC Electives
DTC Electives (12 credits): Any DTC course not included in the degree requirements is eligible to be a DTC elective.

DTC 491

DTC 497 [CAPS]

DTC 498 or 435

Senior Exit Survey

This option is focused on moving image creation and critical cinema commentary. This option focuses on the examination of the history, production, and cultural impact of time-based technologies like sound, film, and animation. Courses in this option explore topics like podcasting, soundscapes, 3D animation, cinema history, video production, and related media. 

This option is available on the Pullman campus. A student may be admitted to the DTC – Digital Cinema, Sound, and Animation Option upon making their intention known to the department. This option requires 42 credits of major-specific coursework.
